contract: Play Matroska, MOV/MP4, TS188 and M2TS192 through Player and the PGS, DVD and DVB subtitle bridges. The pinned FFmpeg subtitles build demuxes the same track and calls avcodec_decode_subtitle2. The plain link serves future measurement.

Fold each published bitmap event, its presentation clock, rectangle count, geometry, forced flag, every declared ARGB palette entry and every visible index row. DVD also compares start and end display offsets. The DVB queue exposes its presentation clock without a display duration; Matroska block DTS is absent at the source boundary, so the reference's inferred DTS is diagnostic only.

For Matroska DVB, buffer through the first selected packet, replay it through the startup clock, then continue with the live clock. Require matching selection, packet identity, payload and known presentation time against the direct Matroska binding. Decode and grade the clock-projected packets.

Check the PGS queue action against the paired decoder event and original packet clock, including show and clear. Check PGS and DVD resets with a pending real packet, a zero work grant, refusal and return of the previous-generation packet, and admission of the new generation.

Compare DVB through the bitmap queue boundary: the first eight decoder rectangles in order, zero for the unanchored queue clock, and the first encoded 33-bit epoch for transport DVB. The trace retains the uncapped decoded event and its clock.
Unprobed Matroska PGS playback compares clocks before generic stream discovery and timestamp fill-in.
Compare MP4 DVD packet clocks on the sample-table timeline with edit mapping disabled in the reference.

Matroska PGS startup cases fold the projected packet clock, duration and complete bytes before decode. The reference consumes public pre-probe packet clocks and applies the same caller-selected prefix boundary and duration-based clock projection. Raw packet clocks remain in the trace. Include explicit selections for both DVB service descriptor arrangements.
Preload the container on both sides. Opening and reading the container, decoding, folding and teardown are inside the operation.

open_deviations.reading: Only the signalled service's composition and ancillary pages are decoded
open_deviations.clause: ETSI EN 300 468 V1.18.1 section 6.2.41: the subtitling descriptor names the composition page and the ancillary page of each service; the PMT here signals one service.
open_deviations.candidate: Uses the ancillary page that follows the signalled composition page and emits one rectangle (5 10 10 24 4 0 16); emits nothing for the other-page and unsignalled-page sources.
open_deviations.reference: Without a dvb_substream option decodes every page: a clear with no rectangle for the ancillary-after and other-page sources, a picture from the unsignalled page 7/8/9. With dvb_substream=0 it agrees with the candidate on all three files.

open_deviations.reading: The first of two DVB subtitling descriptors stays selectable; the reference cannot be asked for it
open_deviations.clause: ETSI EN 300 468 V1.18.1 section 6.2.41: each subtitling descriptor of the PMT signals a service; nothing makes a later descriptor replace an earlier one.
open_deviations.candidate: With descriptor 0 and dvb_substream=0 decodes the first descriptor's service: clears at 1, 2, 3 and 4 s.
open_deviations.reference: Keeps only the later descriptor in the stream's extradata, so dvb_substream=0 decodes the second descriptor's service, which has no events (descriptor 1 gives nothing on both sides): the two sides decode different services.

pending_module_requirements: A Matroska S_VOBSUB track without CodecPrivate is decoded with the DVD receiver's default canvas and palette, as triergon_subtitles::compat::dvd::Decoder decodes such a stream: Matroska codec mappings draft 21 section 3.5.13 says what CodecPrivate holds, not that it is required, and RFC 9559 makes CodecPrivate optional.

DvbTsBridge reports a DVB subtitle PES whose PES_packet_length is 0 as Error::Invalid instead of dropping it with neither output nor error: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) section 2.4.3.7 allows length 0 only for video in a transport stream.

The PAT and PMT readers ignore the reserved bits before a PID and before program_info_length and ES_info_length, and a table refused for any other reason surfaces as a typed error rather than as an absent stream: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) section 2.1 requires encoders to set reserved bits to 1, which constrains the bitstream, not its readers.

open_cases.requirement: A Matroska S_VOBSUB track without CodecPrivate is decoded with the DVD receiver's default canvas and palette, as triergon_subtitles::compat::dvd::Decoder decodes such a stream: Matroska codec mappings draft 21 section 3.5.13 says what CodecPrivate holds, not that it is required, and RFC 9559 makes CodecPrivate optional.

DvbTsBridge reports a DVB subtitle PES whose PES_packet_length is 0 as Error::Invalid instead of dropping it with neither output nor error: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) section 2.4.3.7 allows length 0 only for video in a transport stream.

The PAT and PMT readers ignore the reserved bits before a PID and before program_info_length and ES_info_length, and a table refused for any other reason surfaces as a typed error rather than as an absent stream: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) section 2.1 requires encoders to set reserved bits to 1, which constrains the bitstream, not its readers.

open_refusals.reason: The default DVB binding needs one subtitling service
open_refusals.clause: ETSI EN 300 468 V1.18.1 section 6.2.41 lists every subtitling service of a PID and leaves the choice to the receiver; DvbTsBridge::new requires a single service descriptor for the PID and refuses otherwise with Unsupported; DvbTsBridge::new_for_service decodes one service a caller identifies.
open_refusals.detail: DVB bridge requires one subtitling service
